facts.text: Timekeeper advertises rosgraph_msgs/Clock on the absolute /clock topic with queue size 1.
Timekeeper initializes simulated time to ros::Time(0, 0) and, on StepTime, advances it by max_step_size_ before publishing the clock.
ServiceManager registers the relative pause and resume services on its node handle.
ServiceManager::Pause and ServiceManager::Resume take std_srvs/Empty requests, call World::Pause/World::Resume and return true.
World::Pause sets service_paused_, World::Resume clears it, and World::IsPaused is also true while the internal marker manager is manipulating.
World::Update skips the before-physics plugin hook, the Box2D step and Timekeeper::StepTime while IsPaused is true; only int_marker_manager_.update() still runs.
The flatland_server node defaults update_rate to 200 Hz and step_size to 1/200 s, each overridable by a ROS parameter.
SimulationManager sets Timekeeper's maximum step size from step_size_ before the loop.
The simulation loop sleeps for positive remaining expected-cycle time unless benchmarking.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording fake with no physics step or pacing; placeholder clock samples do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers the declared /clock, /pause and /resume endpoints and runs no Flatland or Box2D physics, plugins, contacts, sensors or wall-clock loop
the clock samples are placeholders and do not advance with the simulator's real time; a live run must receive /clock from the operator's flatland_server
upstream update_rate 200 Hz and step_size 1/200 s are configurable ROS defaults, recorded only as source facts; this fake has no physics timestep or wall-clock pacing
the package exposes no world step, reset, snapshot or restore; only the clock observation and the pause/resume services are in scope
World::IsPaused is also true while the internal marker manager is manipulating, so a held clock sample alone does not prove that the pause service set the flag
